content.text:
I would fix the shared declaration styling before adopting a library for this complaint.

The project already has a component library. `DeclarationList`, `DeclarationCard`, and `ValueRow` compose both member and funder declarations. Features own formatted amounts and content; shared UI owns presentation. See [MemberDeclarations.svelte](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/MemberDeclarations.svelte:14), [FunderDeclarations.svelte](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/FunderDeclarations.svelte:14), and [UI ownership contract](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/lib/ui/README.md:5).

The likely source of the awkward backgrounds is the shared surface composition. `DeclarationCard` renders an unpainted list item with a top border. Each nested `ValueRow` independently paints `--surface`, adds horizontal padding and a bottom divider. This produces inset rectangular strips beneath headings sitting directly on the page canvas. That is an inference from CSS, not a verified visual diagnosis. See [patterns.css](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/lib/ui/patterns.css:287) and [ValueRow.svelte](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/lib/ui/ValueRow.svelte:6).

[PR 108](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/108/files) changes palette tokens and hardcoded colors but preserves that composition. Its neutral light theme uses canvas `#f5f5f4`, surface `#fafafa`, and general line `#8a8a8a`. The declaration container uses the general line, while its internal rows use a quieter divider. Adjusting palette alone leaves the fundamental grouping decision unresolved.

My recommended correction is one explicit declaration pattern. Choose either a full painted card containing heading and entries, or a flat list with transparent entries and restrained dividers. Give declaration surfaces and decorative dividers clear semantic ownership. Avoid using a strong general border token interchangeably for control boundaries and decorative separators. Both feature screens then improve through the same shared change.

Verification also has a relevant gap. The new theme test supplies `declarations: []`, then checks fields and search states. It cannot catch how populated declaration groups look. See [theme.spec.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/tests/theme.spec.ts:73). Add populated member and funder declaration views to visual verification in both themes.

A styled library could help if you want to adopt its full visual language across controls, typography, spacing and surfaces. It still requires designing the bespoke declaration composition and migrating the existing components. A headless library would address interaction behavior but leave these backgrounds to your CSS. For the reported issue, that migration appears larger than the missing design decision.

Caveat for citations: local `tokens.css` contains an older purple light palette despite the branch name matching PR 108. Exact neutral palette values above come from the fetched PR diff. No files changed or tests run.
